reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue lies in the disjunction between qualification performance and historical coefficient weighting. In UEFA-style seeding, teams are assigned to pots based on their historical coefficients, which may not reflect current performance. This creates a paradox where a team that qualifies better (higher rank) can end up in a worse seed (pot) due to a lower historical coefficient. The paper constructs a concrete example showing this inversion. The remedy involves adjusting coefficients such that each team receives the maximum coefficient among those ranked below them in qualification. This ensures that better qualification performance cannot lead to a worse seed, restoring monotonicity. The mathematical structure is a mapping from ordinal qualification ranks to categorical seeding pots, constrained by a non-monotonic coefficient function. The proof relies on constructing a counterexample and then proving the adjusted function is monotone. This is a critical insight for GSE’s design of competitive systems where incentive alignment is paramount.
